name: mixed_lineages_st19_st34
mechanism: A SNP cohort contains both ST19 and ST34 Salmonella Typhimurium isolates submitted as a single clonal population. ST34 differs from ST19 by a single MLST allele (aroC) and a broader set of accessory genome differences. The inter-lineage SNP density (~100-300 SNPs) is orders of magnitude higher than the expected within-outbreak range (~0-20 SNPs). Tools like Gubbins interpret high-density SNP clusters as recombination imports rather than lineage divergence: the inter-lineage SNPs are systematically misclassified as recombinant blocks, r/m estimates are wildly inflated, and the recombination-corrected phylogeny may invert true cluster relationships. The pipeline exits 0 with a plausible-looking tree.

known_behaviors.behavior: Classifies the ST19/ST34 divergence positions as recombinant blocks spanning hundreds of kb. Reports r/m >> 1 (often 5-20x inflated). The resulting recombination-masked phylogeny may show ST19 and ST34 isolates interleaved or collapsed rather than in two distinct clades.

Similar to Gubbins: inter-lineage divergence is modelled as frequent gene conversion events. r/m estimates are unreliable. MCMC may not converge on datasets with this level of between-group divergence.
Produces a valid core alignment with elevated SNP count. Exit 0. The inflation of apparent diversity is not flagged.

samples.description: Salmonella Typhimurium LT2 — canonical complete Typhimurium reference

curation.notes: ST19 samples from PulseNet PRJNA230403 (confirmed serovar=Typhimurium in BioSample). ST34 samples from PRJEB50816 (confirmed serovar=Typhimurium; ST34 confirmed by search metadata). The challenge has 2 ST19 + 2 ST34 samples so Gubbins sees a bimodal SNP density distribution that it cannot distinguish from recombination.
